A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EMMA and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete end matter. v1 has no appendix; v3 includes Appendix A. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, although one benchmark description is inconsistent.

before.justification: v1 reports original EMMA experiments on planning, detection, road graph estimation, scene understanding, and multitask training, including numerical comparisons and ablations in Section 3.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds PaLI-based and chain-of-thought planning results, distant-object detection results, failure examples, and a preliminary inference-speed measurement.

M1.justification: v3 adds a PaLI-X backbone variant and reports a latency-optimized configuration using shorter action sequences, removal of explicit reasoning chains, and strategies such as SARA-RT. The central text representation, task formulations, four-part rationale, and generalist training procedure remain unchanged. Newly documented prompts and meta-decision categories clarify existing components.

E1.justification: The nominal coverage remains nuScenes, WOMD, WOD, and internal driving datasets; NAVSIM is discussed but not evaluated. However, v1 Table 1 explicitly reports WOMD results, whereas the corresponding v3 Table 2 calls its setting an internal planning benchmark despite appearing under the WOMD section. The PDFs do not resolve whether the evaluated data changed.

E2.justification: The nuScenes comparison removes DriveVLM-Dual, whose average L2 was 0.31 in v1 Table 2, while retaining DriveVLM, OmniDrive, and the other comparators in v3 Table 3. Appendix A.5 additionally compares inference speed against UniAD, previously used only for planning accuracy. MotionLM, Wayformer, and the detection comparators remain represented.

E3.justification: v3 introduces PaLI-X and additional CoT configurations into the planning comparison and an FPS evaluation for the optimized variant. Its planning table reports only 1-, 3-, and 5-second horizons, dropping the 8-second column. ADE headings become L2 headings without establishing whether the calculation changed. Newly disclosed dataset counts and sampling intervals do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds three failure analyses covering inadequate motorbike clearance, delayed vehicle detection, and a missed lane merge. Appendix A.2 extends the detection breakdown beyond 50 metres, while Table 2 adds backbone and CoT comparisons. The original trajectory-sampling, data-scaling, CoT-component, road-graph, scene-understanding, and co-training analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: The co-training table retains the same standard-deviation reporting and values from v1 Table 4 to v3 Table 5. Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures, and v3 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 substantially extends the result set with PaLI/CoT planning rows, beyond-50-metre detection results, failure findings, and a reported 3 FPS versus UniAD's 1.8 FPS. Table 2 adds EMMA+ with CoT at 0.543 for 5-second L2 and revises baseline entries, including Wayformer's 5-second value from 0.640 to 0.628; benchmark and metric ambiguities prevent treating these as uniform same-setting improvements. Eight-second results disappear. nuScenes EMMA+ remains at 0.29 average L2; the new 12.1% comparison uses OmniDrive's 0.33 instead of the earlier 6.4% comparison against DriveVLM-Dual's 0.31.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, the autoregressive probability formulation, coordinate representations, and dataset-proportional training formulation retain their mathematical substance. Neither version contains theoretical guarantees or proofs, and v3 adds none.

C1.justification: The introduction broadens EMMA from a Gemini-based system to a framework compatible with foundation models such as Gemini and PaLI. The four principal contributions concerning planning, perception, generalist co-training, and long-tail reasoning otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds specific qualifications about nuScenes collision-metric sensitivity and easily extrapolated trajectories, hypothesizes that camera resolution explains reduced distant-object advantages, and discusses consequences of concrete failures. Existing memory, sensing, and verification limitations mostly move to Appendix A.5. The earlier explanation of weaker 8-second planning disappears, while deployment discussion gains a cautiously positive interpretation of the optimized variant.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 and Table 1 disclose exact training-example counts, driving hours, and internal-data sampling intervals that were previously largely unspecified. Section 2.2 and Appendix Tables 6–7 supply caption-generation prompts, all 12 speed-based meta-decision categories, and concrete generalist prompts and outputs. These materially improve specification of the existing pipeline. Conversely, v1's explicit disclosure that WOMD camera inputs were internally supplied and unavailable in the released dataset is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 expands discussion of self-supervision through EmerNeRF, Copilot4D, and JointMotion, and adds driving frameworks including PARA-Drive, GenAD, LMDrive, and DriveCoT. Robotics applications, NAVSIM, and SARA-RT also broaden the context. The central positioning of EMMA as an end-to-end generalist MLLM remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 introduces a dataset-overview subsection and structured appendix, moves limitations from Section 5 to Appendix A.5, and shortens the abstract and conclusion. It also makes localized wording, heading, and authorship edits. Most method exposition, contribution bullets, and experimental explanations remain recognizable rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different TMLR layout and reworks Figures 1–2. The original detection Figure 5 is reorganized into an enlarged aggregate comparison and Appendix Figure 11, which also adds distant-range panels. New dataset, meta-decision, and prompt tables and a failure-example figure expand the visual presentation; planning-table rows and columns are also restructured.

improvement.justification: The added dataset and prompt documentation, backbone experiments, distant-object results, and concrete failure analyses improve transparency and diagnostic value. However, v3 removes the 8-second results, DriveVLM-Dual comparison, and private-WOMD-image disclosure while inconsistently identifying Table 2's benchmark. The nuScenes caption also retains the old 6.4% comparison despite the changed comparator discussion. These competing changes leave central benchmark comparability insufficiently clear to establish a reliable net improvement or deterioration.
